newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs likely to start bourse trade mid-June.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs likely to start bourse trade mid-June.

text.p: Poland's National Investment Funds (NFIs) will likely start trade on the main market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange in mid-June, the bourse's president said.

"The bourse's board received all (necessary) applications from the NFIs. They will be evaluated by mid-May and then the bourse's management will determine the (exact) day of the first listing. We are aiming for the middle of June," Wieslaw Rozlucki told a news conference.
Rozlucki added that all NFIs must present their audited 1996 results in the first days of June in order to keep on track for a mid-June first listing.
He said there was no specified amount of NFI units which had to be exchanged into shares of the 15 investment funds in order to launch the NFIs listing.
"We will not set a limit because then investors may wait until this limit is surpassed," Rozlucki said.

Under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, owners of Poland's nearly 27 million NFI units have until the end of 1998 to exchange these units into 15 NFIs shares, one share for each of the investment funds.
Rozlucki said that the NFIs listing would add about $1.4 billion to the Warsaw bourse's current market capitalisation of $10 billion.
